what:
dedup (one way per job): two runtimes patch a running program. blaze-inproc is v2 (compile-time.md change 6, fastcompile/inproc.md): one shared code memory, a word store makes code reachable, fences retire old code, no mprotect and no stopped threads; blaze-cargo dev runs use it (serve/unit/run/inproc.rs). blaze-live keeps its own: Live::start maps each patch next to the program and either writes jumps over function entries with every other thread stopped (src/apply.rs, the v1 path its own doc calls v1) or uses the slots runtime (src/slots*). Its users are harness/live*, live-bevy, live-egui (Live::start/poll) and, for the patch message only, blaze-link and blaze-cargo (blaze_live::patch).
Ask: make Live::start/poll a thin user API over blaze_inproc (attach, runtime::quiesce at poll, the fence), keep blaze_live::patch as the one message format (or move it into blaze-link), and delete apply.rs and the map-and-jump path with its platform modules. If the stop-the-world path is a different job (a program not started by blaze, no BLAZE_INPROC), say so with the case and dedup records it as kept. Tier-up sampling (sample.rs, tiers) stays with whichever runtime owns the process.
